sermon.title: How to Meet with Jesus
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer establishes that Jesus died for the world and for the church that sins, and invites everyone to come to him for rest, free of man-made religious burdens. Using the tabernacle, he shows we enter God’s presence boldly by the blood and come in with thanksgiving and praise, which God inhabits. Believers are the chosen generation created to praise him, and meeting God strengthens and compels us.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Psalm 100:4 spoken as “Psalms 104”; Psalm 22:3 spoken as “Psalms 20 23”; “12 stages of the cross”; the late-1940s awakening revealing entry by praise; Job dated near Abraham. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Catholics crawling to church doing penance; groups requiring tongues for salvation; dietary laws, dress and hair rules; holy water sold.

faqs.question: Did Jesus die for the church’s sins too?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the church that sins and for the whole world.

faqs.question: What labor and burden does Matthew 11:28 mean?
faqs.answer: The burden of your spirit, not work or chores.

faqs.question: Must you speak in tongues to be saved?
What makes a person spiritual?
faqs.answer: Working on the inner man and following Jesus.

faqs.question: Will Jesus cast out anyone who comes?

faqs.answer: No, he comes to talk to you and change your life.
